name: Celebrity or public-figure impersonation in a social-media investment funnel
description: An investment approach on social media leans on an impersonated celebrity or public figure, fake testimonials and unrealistic returns. NARROWED (2026-08-28): the deepfake-specific mechanism is excluded — SEBI's release verifies celebrity/public-figure impersonation but contains no deepfake statement (G-16 stays open).

source_references.document_ref: SEBI PR No. 27/2025 — stock-market scams via social media

manual_retrieval.notes: Body now retrieved (was PRIMARY_CITED_UNVERIFIED). Verifies celebrity/public-figure impersonation, fake testimonials and unreasonable-return promises. Contains NO deepfake-specific statement — the deepfake mechanism is narrowed out and stays an open gap (G-16).

explanation.plain: This investment pitch uses a famous person's name or image to look trustworthy. Celebrities do not run investment tips through social-media DMs, and 'endorsements' like these are usually fake. Treat guaranteed-return claims tied to a celebrity as a scam.
explanation.technical: CELEBRITY_IMPERSONATION (identity-claim) with an investment solicitation or return claim (financial/pretext). SEBI PR 27/2025 verifies the celebrity-impersonation funnel; the deepfake variant is not covered.
verification_steps: Check whether the 'endorsement' appears on the celebrity's genuine, verified account.
Only deal with SEBI-registered intermediaries; verify the registration number.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: SEBI's body verifies celebrity impersonation but not a deepfake mechanism, so the rule is narrowed to impersonation and capped at PARTIAL. The deepfake-specific detection remains an open gap (G-16). Held at PEER_REVIEW.
